title: Women in the Bible: what does the Bible say?
opening_question: What does the Bible say about women? Read it from the beginning: how God made the woman, the prophetesses and women of faith in Israel, the virtuous woman, Mary, the women who followed Jesus and saw Him risen, the women of the early church, what Paul writes about women in the churches with the verses around it, and what all are in Christ. Read every verse, also the ones that seem to point another way, and let the text speak.

steps.question: In whose image did God make man, male and female? Why did God make the woman, and what did Adam call her?

facts.text: "man" in Genesis 1:27 is the Hebrew 'adam, "a human being" or "the species mankind". The same verse says "male and female created he them", and both are told to "have dominion".
Strong's gives 'ezer, "aid", for "help" in Genesis 2:18. The Bible uses the same word for God Himself: "My help cometh from the LORD" and "he is our help and our shield".
"Eve" is the Hebrew Chavvah, "lifegiver": Adam called her so "because she was the mother of all living".

steps.question: Who led the women of Israel in song, whom did the LORD send before Israel with Moses and Aaron, who judged Israel, to whom did the priest go to enquire of the LORD, and who published the word in Psalm 68?

facts.text: "prophetess" is the Hebrew nebiy'ah, "a prophetess or (generally) inspired woman". The text gives that name to Miriam, Deborah and Huldah.
Barak would not go to battle without Deborah. She went, and said the LORD would "sell Sisera into the hand of a woman".
Deborah calls herself "a mother in Israel".

"those that published it" in Psalm 68:11 is one Hebrew word, ha-mevasserot, from basar, "to announce (glad news)". Its ending -ot is feminine plural: women who bring the news. So the BSB says "a great company of women proclaim it"; the KJV and the Ethiopian Canon don't show the women. The Hebrew line of the verse (under Look closer) has the word.

steps.question: What did Ruth promise Naomi, and what did the women of Bethlehem say when Ruth's son was born? What did Hannah pray, how did Sarah conceive, and what did Esther risk?

facts.text: "virtuous" in Ruth 3:11 is chayil, the same Hebrew word as in "Who can find a virtuous woman?" Strong's gives "virtue", "valor" and "strength" among its meanings.
Hannah calls herself "thine handmaid" three times in one prayer, and says afterwards: "For this child I prayed".
Sarah "received strength to conceive seed" when she was past age, "because she judged him faithful who had promised".
When Ruth's son was born, the women said to Naomi "Blessed be the LORD", and called Ruth "better to thee than seven sons".

steps.question: Who can find a virtuous woman? What does she do with her hands, her mouth and her household? What adorning is of great price in the sight of God, and which women does Peter hold up as examples?

facts.text: The virtuous woman "considereth a field, and buyeth it", "planteth a vineyard", "maketh fine linen, and selleth it" and "stretcheth out her hand to the poor".
"meek" in 1 Peter 3:4 is praus, "mild"; "quiet" is hesuchios, "still (undisturbed, undisturbing)".

Peter holds up "the holy women also, who trusted in God", and Sarah, who "obeyed Abraham, calling him lord". He writes to wives whose husbands "obey not the word", that they "may without the word be won". The study Husband and wife reads these verses with Ephesians 5 and Colossians 3.

steps.question: What did the angel tell Mary, what did she answer, what did Elisabeth say of her faith, and to whom did Jesus give His mother at the cross?

facts.text: "handmaid" in Luke 1:38 and "handmaiden" in Luke 1:48 is the Greek doule, "a female slave (involuntarily or voluntarily)". Mary gives herself the lowest name.
"blessed is she that believed": Elisabeth blesses Mary for her faith.

steps.question: Which women travelled with Jesus and ministered to Him, which sister chose that good part, whose word brought a Samaritan city to believe, and what did Jesus call the woman He healed?

facts.text: "ministered" in Luke 8:3 is diakoneo, "to be an attendant, i.e. wait upon". The women ministered to Him "of their substance".
Mary "sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word". Paul uses the same picture for his own schooling: brought up "at the feet of Gamaliel".
To the woman at the well Jesus said "I that speak unto thee am he". His disciples "marvelled that he talked with the woman".

steps.question: Who stood by the cross, who came to the sepulchre on the first day of the week, and to whom did the risen Jesus say "go to my brethren"?

facts.text: Luke names the women who told the apostles: "Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James". At first "their words seemed to them as idle tales".
"Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord".
Many women followed Jesus from Galilee, "ministering unto him", and stood "beholding afar off" at the cross.

steps.question: Who prayed with the apostles before Pentecost, on whom did God say He would pour out His Spirit, and which women served the church in Acts and in Paul's letters?

facts.text: On the day of Pentecost Peter quotes the prophet Joel: "your sons and your daughters shall prophesy", and "on my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my Spirit".
"servant" in Romans 16:1 is diakonos, "an attendant"; Strong's adds "(technically, a deacon or deaconess)". The KJV translates the word "deacon, minister, servant".
"helpers" in Romans 16:3 is synergos, "a co-laborer". Priscilla and Aquila together "expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly".

Romans 16:7 says Andronicus and Junia "are of note among the apostles"; the BSB says "outstanding among the apostles". Readers differ on whether this means they were counted among the apostles or were well known to them.

steps.question: What does Paul write about a woman who prays or prophesies, about silence in the churches, about teaching, and about what the aged women teach? Read every verse in full, with the verses around it, side by side.

facts.text: In 1 Corinthians 11:5 a woman "prayeth or prophesieth"; in 14:34 Paul writes "Let your women keep silence in the churches". Christians read these verses together in different ways. The path shows them all; the commentary below is labelled as the words of men.

The verses around 1 Corinthians 14:34 are about order when the church comes together: "Let all things be done unto edifying", "ye may all prophesy one by one", "God is not the author of confusion, but of peace", "Let all things be done decently and in order".

Paul grounds what he writes in Genesis: "the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man" and "Adam was first formed, then Eve". In the same chapter he adds: "even so is the man also by the woman; but all things of God".
1 Timothy is a letter to Timothy, whom Paul left "at Ephesus" to "charge some that they teach no other doctrine".
"silence" in 1 Timothy 2:11-12 is hesuchia, "stillness"; the KJV has the same word as "quietness" in 2 Thessalonians 3:12. "silence" in 1 Corinthians 14:34 is another word, sigao, "to keep silent".
"usurp authority" in 1 Timothy 2:12 is authenteo, "to act of oneself", "dominate". Strong's counts it only once in the New Testament.
The aged women are to be "teachers of good things", that "they may teach the young women".
In the same chapter Paul writes: "neither is the man without the woman, neither the woman without the man, in the Lord".

steps.question: What are all who are baptized into Christ, and what are husband and wife together?

facts.text: "male" and "female" in Galatians 3:28 are the Greek arsen and thelus, the same words Jesus uses when He goes back to the beginning: "made them male and female".
"heirs together" in 1 Peter 3:7 is one Greek word, synkleronomos, "a co-heir".
